title: Rock falling into lava: does the turned piece settle or stick?
question: In the last tile, one pane has a dark clump resting at the lava/water boundary that the other does not. Does that read as a piece correctly settling on the lava, or as a piece stuck where it should have tumbled free?
context_md:
Fixing `open-bugs-handoff.md` bug K. The rotation-fit probe was **vacuous**: it handed each cell its own position, so it always answered "clear" and a body rotated a quarter turn *unconditionally* — including straight through a wall it was wedged against. Present in both parents of the water merge, and invisible, because a probe that always says "clear" looks exactly like one that works.

The fix makes a body refuse the turn when the turned shape would land in rock.

**What I already measured, so you don't have to:** 17 of 21 acceptance cases have *identical* peak body counts. No new test or acceptance failures. No frame cost — apparent timing swings were machine noise, proved by zero-body cases moving as much as body cases.

**What I am unsure of, and why I am asking:** the fix makes bodies rotate *less*, so a piece could now be stuck in a pose it would previously have turned out of. The clump at the lava line is the one visible difference and I cannot tell from a still whether it is right.

items.label: after — turn refused when it would land in rock
items.caption: wedged bodies keep their orientation
